summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of recurrent nausea and vomiting was admitted after failing to tolerate oral intake despite initial ED management. She was found to have hypokalemia and a positive urine analysis, though the culture later indicated contamination. Treatment focused on rehydration, correcting electrolytes, and managing nausea. Based on prior endoscopy showing H. pylori gastritis, she was started on a two-week course of amoxicillin and levofloxacin with omeprazole. An ultrasound showed no liver abnormalities, but further workup for esophageal varices was pending. Her mood was low during admission, prompting continued sertraline and social support. She improved, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home with follow-up in primary care and gastroenterology.
